# Importer {#sec-importer}

The importer is found in `source/backend/core/importer/importer.py`. It reads a circuit
written in **OpenQASM 2 or 3** and returns a Qiskit `QuantumCircuit`. It is **not**
a stage of the pipeline: `compile` receives the circuit it returns, like any
other circuit. It is exported from `backend` for convenience:
`from backend import load_circuit`.

## Why it is needed {.unnumbered}

The viewer used to list a few example circuits. A circuit that a person writes
must go through the whole platform (transpilation, translation to native gates,
simulation and metrics) before it reaches the JSON contract, so the viewer does
not load JSON files in Qollab any more: it loads circuits. OpenQASM is the
standard text format for them, and the organizers of the hackathon recommended it.

## `load_circuit(text)` {.unnumbered}

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | The circuit. The first statement must be `OPENQASM 2.0;` or `OPENQASM 3.0;` (comments and a UTF-8 BOM before it are allowed). |

**Returns** a `QuantumCircuit`.

- OpenQASM 2 is read with `qiskit.qasm2.loads`, which comes with Qiskit.
- OpenQASM 3 is read with `qiskit.qasm3.loads`, which needs the package
  `qiskit-qasm3-import` (MIT-compatible: Apache-2.0, with `openqasm3` and
  `antlr4-python3-runtime`, which are pure Python). It is imported only when a
  circuit in OpenQASM 3 is loaded, so OpenQASM 2 keeps working if it is missing.

**Raises**

| Exception | When |
| --- | --- |
| `CircuitParseError` | The text is empty, longer than `config.MAX_QASM_CHARS` (200 000 characters), has no valid header, uses a version other than 2 or 3, or has a syntax or semantic error. The message keeps the line and column of the parser. |
| `UnsupportedOperationError` | The circuit has control flow (`if`, `for`, `while`, `switch`), which a step-by-step view cannot show, or an `opaque` gate, which has no definition to translate. |

The limits that depend on the machine are not checked here. `compile` rejects
more qubits than the limit (`CircuitTooLargeError`), mid-circuit measurements and
`reset`, and parameters without a value (`input float theta;`), with
`UnsupportedOperationError`. Final measurements (`c = measure q;`) are accepted
and removed, as for any circuit.

## Loading without spending the IonQ job {.unnumbered}

On IonQ the transpilation asks the machine for its own compilation, and that
spends the single job allowed per run. A person who loads several files cannot
afford it, so `qollab_api.run_qasm` calls `compile(..., allow_remote=False)`:
the circuit is transpiled locally and the job is never sent. The error model
(`metrics`) does not use a job: it works from the fixed profile of the machine.

## In Qollab {.unnumbered}

`qollab_api.run_qasm(backend, qasm, shots, entangler)` reads the text and returns
the JSON text of the visualization. The viewer calls it through `HOST.compileQasm`
(see [the Qollab page](../frontend/qollab.qmd)). The example circuits are in
`resources/examples/qasm/` (`bell.qasm`, `ghz4.qasm`, `qft3.qasm` and `bell_qasm2.qasm`).
